notes: Incremental (warm) numbers are the routine-iteration metric. Cold numbers depend on target/ population and do not govern the wave gate. `.bbnf-cache` cleared before each cold run via `find . -name .bbnf-cache -type d -exec rm -rf {} +`. The target/ symlink points at the main repo's build dir so cold here means `.bbnf-cache` absent, not `target/` nuked — identical framing to the baseline. Baseline columns are copied verbatim from `docs/benchmarks/post-B0-W0-baseline.txt` and have not been re-run.
conclusions: iter-check warm (0.16s) is ~45x faster than baseline workspace-check warm (7.16s), promoting the ~30x gap the baseline flagged into the public command surface.

make iter-test-leaf now produces real pass/fail output (warm 1.05s, cold 48.41s); baseline scripts/test-tier.sh leaf failed in 0.45s with the stale `-p bbnf-tape` crate name before the W0.a alias-crate-list fix.
cargo test --workspace --no-run warm of 0.76s (vs 14.40s baseline) reflects target/ symlink sharing with main — it stays the heavy final-proof surface regardless, correctly outside the routine loop.
make iter-check wraps cargo iter-check with identical cost (0.16s warm), confirming the Makefile target is a transparent wrapper around the alias, not an additional dispatch layer.
